pages.purpose: Shared chrome and engines injected into every page: sticky top bar, floating pill bottom nav, water quick-log, AI-coach button, 'buddy' chat companion, XP/levels/achievements, 5 anime skins, a 10-option surface-style engine and 6 home looks, collapsible/reorderable sections, a jump-to-section drawer, opt-in page tabs, desktop eye-break timer, cross-device settings/water sync and service-worker auto-update. It is 220KB, loaded and parsed on every page. Rough byte split: buddy ~38KB (17%), XP plus its CSS ~31KB, skins/UI-style/home-look definitions and CSS ~50KB+, sections/nav/eyes ~42KB, and the real infrastructure is the rest.
pages.screensOfScrollOnPhone: Not a page, it's chrome. On a notched iPhone (844px tall) about 200px is permanently taken: the sticky top bar is ~95px including safe-area, and the fixed pill nav is ~70px plus the 34px home indicator. A ~70px skin banner sits under the top bar when a skin is on. On top of content float the 56px coach FAB, the 60px buddy disc and a 22x66px left-edge drawer tab. Before any content, roughly 25-30% of the first screen is chrome.
pages.designNotes: The core problem: there is no single designed look, only a theme engine. Seven independent appearance axes stack on top of each other: light/dark, 8 accents, 6 skins (none plus 5 anime), 11 surface styles (default plus 10), 6 home looks, 4 home structures, 3 card radii and 3 font sizes. That is about 57,000 combinations, each built from hundreds of !important overrides on old page class names (.gm-card, .hth-card, .hb-card…). Nothing is fully intentional, which explains why it 'wasn't eye-pulling'. Constant motion: up to 6 infinite animations run at once (coach FAB pulse ring, buddy float and aura spin, banner shimmer, banner name shine, banner mark bob, active-tab pulse). It feels busy rather than premium. Feedback stacking: one water tap fires a button flash, an emoji burst, a buddy speech bubble and an XP toast from the top, plus confetti on level-up. Section headers get an auto-assigned rainbow (24 regex colour rules plus hashed hues) and ↑ ↓ ▾ controls on every header. Inner pages spend a sticky ~95px bar on just 'v2.7.8', a ⭐Lv chip and a gear. The default nav shows every enabled page, up to 10 tabs at 8.5px labels. Old reference screenshots (ss_home.png, ss_health.png) show the June version: a calm 3-tab nav and a minimal top bar, which is the 'before more-and-more' baseline. Genuinely nice and worth reusing: the floating glass pill nav, the 'cinematic' home look (serif 'Good evening, <name>' plus an uppercase date line, hairline glass cards, numbered tiles, cyan glow), the iOS-style XP banner craftsmanship (as a pattern for real insight toasts, not XP), and the solid iOS plumbing (16px input zoom fix, resume-aware SW updates).

features.name: Bottom pill nav (ALL_TABS + More sheet + custom pinning)
features.whatItDoes: Fixed floating pill bar on every page except finance and iframes. Up to 10 tabs (Main, Health, Food, Fitness, School, Habits, Transport, Projects, Friends, Settings), filtered by settings.pages. Optional custom mode pins N tabs and moves the rest into a 'More' bottom sheet. The skin swaps the tab emojis. Finance and Trends have no tab: Finance is reached from the home top bar, Trends from elsewhere.
features.manualInputs: None daily. Optional one-time config in Settings → Navigation bar. With navCustom unset (the default), every visible page gets a tab: up to 10 at ~39px each with 8.5px ellipsised labels.
features.valueReturned: Navigation works. But 10 equal-weight destinations tell the owner 'here are 10 areas to maintain', the opposite of 'save space and complication'.
features.dataKeys: localStorage dashboard:nav:v1 {navCustom, navCount, navPinned} (device-only, never synced); legacy copies of the same fields in dashboard:settings:v1; settings.pages
features.overlapsWith: settings.html navigation section; index.html's own fixed .tabbar; jump-to-section drawer; home 'More' disclosure (v2.7.7)
features.automationPotential: Ship a fixed 4-5 tab set in the redesign (e.g. Today / Body / Money / More) instead of a configurable 10. Pages with no recent data can be auto-demoted into More.

features.name: Top bar (version label + level chip + settings gear; home adds water pill + finance shortcut)
features.whatItDoes: Sticky glass header on every page except settings and finance. Home shows: v2.7.8 · ⭐Lv chip with mini XP bar · water pill and + · 📊 finance link · ⚙️. Every other page shows only v2.7.8 · ⭐Lv chip · ⚙️. Tapping the version 5x opens the diagnostics panel.
features.manualInputs: None
features.valueReturned: On inner pages it spends ~95px of permanent sticky height on a developer version number, a gamification chip and a gear. That is no information.
features.dataKeys: Reads dashboard:xp:v1 and po_water_v1; no keys of its own
features.overlapsWith: Settings tab in the nav (the gear duplicates it); XP chip duplicates the buddy's own 'Lv' pip
features.automationPotential: Remove it on inner pages and let each page have its own title row. On home, replace it with a greeting hero plus 1-line status. Move the version to Settings → About and keep the 5-tap diag hatch there.

features.name: Water quick-log pill (+1 bottle)
features.whatItDoes: Shows today's water as e.g. 1.5/3.2L against a personalised target: weight×35ml, plus activity, plus caffeine above 200mg ×1.5, plus substances, plus sex/age adjustments. A status dot turns amber below 50% and pulses red after 18:00 if still below 50%. '+' adds one 'bottle' (default 500ml) to local storage and merge-pushes it into the cloud health row. It also fires an emoji burst, a buddy bubble and +5 XP (capped at 8/day). Home page only.
features.manualInputs: 1 tap per bottle, ~3-6 taps/day. Profile (weight, age, sex, activity) set once on Health or via a coach tool.
features.valueReturned: The best input-to-value ratio in the whole app: one tap gives instant progress against a target the user never had to calculate.
features.dataKeys: localStorage po_water_v1 ↔ app_state uid:health.po_water_v1 {logs{YYYY-MM-DD: ml}, hist{date:[ml,…]}, sizes{cup,bottle,big}, profile{weightKg,age,sex,activityHrsPerWeek}, caffeineMgPerDay, substances[], bottleMl, glassMl, unit, _mlV2:true}; uid:health._pushAt is the change marker
features.overlapsWith: health.html water section (same data); home dashGrid water tile (v2.7.7); coach tool set_water_setup; buddy hydration nags
features.automationPotential: Keep the one-tap pattern and drop the 3 celebration effects. Water could also be logged with zero app-opening from an iOS Shortcut (Action Button / back-tap / widget) hitting a token GET endpoint like /api/steps, or pulled from Apple Health water entries.

features.name: Floating AI Coach button (🧠 FAB)
features.whatItDoes: 56px accent circle with an infinite pulsing ring, bottom-right on every page except coach and finance; opens coach.html. It is re-inserted at load and after 900ms because other scripts and section-collapse kept removing it.
features.manualInputs: Getting any value means opening the coach and typing a question; the coach never speaks first.
features.valueReturned: One-tap access to the only feature that interprets the owner's data. But it is pull-only, and the pulse ring is permanent visual noise.
features.dataKeys: None (coach.html keeps its own chat history)
features.overlapsWith: Buddy chat (a second chat bubble on every page); health.html food-coach chat (fcChat, also calls /api/coach); settings.html AI test call
features.automationPotential: One assistant entry point. The coach's daily brief should appear on the home screen and in a push notification, so the owner gets the info without asking.

features.name: Buddy companion widget (BUDDY_DEFS / DEFAULT_BUDDY 'Nova')
features.whatItDoes: 60px draggable floating disc with an animated aura, float and 'Lv' pip; tapping opens a 330x460 chat panel. The persona follows the skin (Luffy, Isagi, Monarch, Gojo, Tanjiro, or Nova by default). It is NOT AI: a keyword classifier picks from ~25 canned reply pools and sometimes appends a nudge about goal count, streak or water. Sending a message raises 'affinity' by 1 (a second, different level number). It pops ambient bubbles after water logs and when all goals are done. Quick chips: My week, Motivate me, I'm tired, My goals, Tell a joke.
features.manualInputs: None required; optional typing to a scripted bot
features.valueReturned: Generic motivational lines and jokes. It knows nothing beyond goal count, streak and water. It covers content (a scroll-fade hack was added to get it out of the way), and it competes with the real AI coach.
features.dataKeys: localStorage only, never synced: buddy_chat (last 40 msgs), buddy_affinity, buddy_pos, buddy_recap_week; settings.buddy='off' hides it; reads goals:<date>, goal_streak_v1, dashboard:mood:v1, po_coach_weights, po_water_v1, dashboard:xp:v1
features.overlapsWith: AI coach FAB / coach.html; XP level chip ('Lv' shown twice with different meanings); skin personas
features.automationPotential: None worth keeping except the weekly recap (next item). Removing it deletes ~38KB from every page load.

features.name: Weekly recap ('📊 My week', inside buddy)
features.whatItDoes: Computes the last 7 days: goals done/total, goal streak, average mood, weight change, water logged and XP gained. The water figure is a raw sum that mixes ml and legacy cup counts. It auto-runs on Sundays the first time the buddy chat is opened that week.
features.manualInputs: Open the buddy chat and tap the chip, or happen to open it on a Sunday
features.valueReturned: Exactly the kind of 'track and give me info' summary the owner wants, but buried inside a toy chat most people never open.
features.dataKeys: Reads goals:<date>, goal_streak_v1, dashboard:mood:v1, po_coach_weights, po_water_v1, dashboard:xp:v1; writes buddy_recap_week
features.overlapsWith: summary.html, trends.html, coach
features.automationPotential: Generate it server-side or on first open each Sunday and deliver it as a push plus a home card. Add steps (uid:steps), app usage (uid:screen) and spending. The coach can phrase it in 3 bullets.

features.name: XP & levels (top-bar chip, XP toasts, daily check-in)
features.whatItDoes: Level curve: 100 XP for Lv2, then +18% per level. XP comes from page hooks: +20 'Daily check-in' just for opening, weight +25/day, mood +10/day, habit +15, goal +10, all goals cleared +50, meal +8, food +10, workout +12, water +5 (max 8/day). Every gain slides an iOS-style banner down from the top with a progress bar. Level-ups add confetti and post to friends' activity feed. Tapping the chip opens a modal: level bar, streak freezes, badges, last 6 gains, 'How to earn XP' table. XP also gates skins (settings.html SKIN_LOCK: Blue Lock Lv3, Solo Leveling Lv6, Jujutsu Lv10, Demon Slayer Lv15).
features.manualInputs: None directly, but the system exists to make the owner log more, and the first thing they see each day is a '+20 XP Daily check-in' toast
features.valueReturned: Measures input volume (taps), not outcomes, so it says nothing about health, money or school. It is the 'app felt like a duty' mechanic in its purest form.
features.dataKeys: localStorage dashboard:xp:v1 {total, spent, freezesBought, freezesUsed, maxStreak, curStreak, counts{}, badges{}, log[≤20], claims{}, dayCaps{}, dayCats{}} ↔ app_state uid:xp (max-merge); Supabase profiles.level/xp/xp_week/streak/skin; activity table rows; window.dashAddXp / dashAddXpDaily / dashAddXpCapped called from index, health, habits, gym, food
features.overlapsWith: Buddy affinity 'Lv'; goal/habit streaks on home and habits; gym Strength Rank; friends leaderboard
features.automationPotential: If any progress signal stays, derive it from outcomes (step goal hit, weight trend, budget kept, sleep average) rather than from logging taps. Keep uid:xp in the DB but stop rendering it.

features.name: Achievements (15 badges) + Streak Freeze shop
features.whatItDoes: Badges: First Steps, Lv5/10/25, 10/100 goals, Clean Sweep, 25 habits, 7 weigh-ins, 50 waters, 7 moods, 30 meals, Perfect Day (XP in 5 categories in one day), 7/30-day goal streak. An unlock fires a gold toast, confetti and a friends activity post. Streak Freeze costs 150 spendable XP and is auto-consumed by index.html when a goal day is missed.
features.manualInputs: Occasional 'Buy · 150 XP' tap in the XP modal
features.valueReturned: Adds streak anxiety and collection pressure; returns no information.
features.dataKeys: dashboard:xp:v1.badges / .spent / .freezesBought / .freezesUsed / .maxStreak (synced in uid:xp); window.dashGetFreezes / dashUseFreeze / dashNoteStreak used by index.html
features.overlapsWith: XP system; goal streak on home
features.automationPotential: None needed

features.name: Friends presence + profile/activity broadcast
features.whatItDoes: If a friend_profile exists, it updates the Supabase profiles row (level, xp, xp_week, streak, skin, updated_at) after every XP change and every 2 minutes while visible (a presence heartbeat). It inserts activity rows on level-ups and badge unlocks.
features.manualInputs: None
features.valueReturned: Broadcasts gamification stats to friends, which adds social comparison pressure rather than useful sharing. It also costs a Supabase write every 2 minutes.
features.dataKeys: localStorage friend_profile; Supabase tables profiles, activity
features.overlapsWith: friends.html
features.automationPotential: If Friends survives, share opt-in outcome highlights (e.g. weekly steps) instead of XP; drop the 2-minute heartbeat.

features.name: Skin engine (SKIN_DEFS: One Piece, Blue Lock, Solo Leveling, Jujutsu Kaisen, Demon Slayer)
features.whatItDoes: Each skin swaps the accent pair, a Google display font (Bangers/Orbitron/Oxanium/Cinzel…), a background gradient plus SVG pattern, the nav emojis and the buddy persona. It also adds: a rotating character banner under the top bar (emoji, name, quote; changes every 5.5s with shimmer), a 1.5s full-screen splash when switching, a light sweep on every page load, a once-per-session welcome toast on home, emoji bursts on water log, glowing gradient section titles and a pulsing active tab.
features.manualInputs: One-time pick in Settings; higher skins locked behind XP levels
features.valueReturned: The closest thing to 'eye-pulling' and personality in the app. But it is a costume over unchanged generic pages: a ~70px banner on every page, constant motion, an extra font download, and display fonts that hurt the legibility of numbers.
features.dataKeys: dashboard:settings:v1.skin ↔ uid:settings; sessionStorage skinWelcome:<skin>; profiles.skin
features.overlapsWith: settings.html skin cards plus its SKIN_VIS anti-flash map; buddy personas; surface-style and home-look engines; accent colours
features.automationPotential: Fold the personality into one designed theme, e.g. an optional accent or a single signature character moment on the home hero. Drop the banner, splash, sweep, toast and bursts.

features.name: Surface-style engine (uiStyle ×10) + Dashboard 'home look' ×6 + accent/cardStyle/fontSize/homeStructure
features.whatItDoes: 10 surface styles (skeuomorphism, neomorphism, glassmorphism, claymorphism, minimalism, maximalism, brutalism, liquid glass, bento, spatial) restyle every card, input and button via !important CSS variables. 6 home looks (classic, cinematic, neon, aurora, ember, mono) restyle the home page and chrome, and non-classic looks add the greeting. On top of that: 8 accents, light/dark, 3 card radii, 3 font sizes and 4 home structures (classic/compact/grid/bento).
features.manualInputs: One-time picks in Settings, but the option count invites endless fiddling instead of using the app
features.valueReturned: ~57k untested combinations instead of one finished design. Every option overrides legacy class names, so none looks fully intentional. The cinematic look is the best of them and a good seed for the redesign.
features.dataKeys: dashboard:settings:v1 {theme, accent, uiStyle, home, homeStructure, cardStyle, fontSize} ↔ uid:settings; constants UI_BG, UI_BG_LIGHT, HOME_BG; html attributes data-ui, data-home, data-home-structure, data-skin, data-theme
features.overlapsWith: Skin engine; settings.html pickers; index.html home-structure CSS
features.automationPotential: Pick one look (dark, cinematic-like, one accent) and maybe keep light/dark. The redesign can simply ignore the old fields, with no data migration needed.

features.name: Personal greeting header ('Good evening, <name>' + date)
features.whatItDoes: On non-classic home looks, replaces 'My Dashboard' with a time-of-day greeting, the user's name and an uppercase weekday/date line.
features.manualInputs: Name once (onboarding/settings)
features.valueReturned: A warm, personal first impression with no input; the most premium-feeling text in the app.
features.dataKeys: settings.name, settings.home
features.overlapsWith: index.html .dash-title
features.automationPotential: Make it the default hero and add one auto-generated status line beneath it (e.g. '6.2k steps · 1.5/3.2L · ₪140 left this week').

features.name: Collapsible + reorderable sections
features.whatItDoes: Every .section-title on every page except settings and finance gets ↑ ↓ ▾ controls. Tapping the header collapses the section; arrows reorder it. State is saved per page, per device.
features.manualInputs: Manually arranging and collapsing each page, separately on each device (not synced)
features.valueReturned: Lets the owner hide clutter by hand. It is a workaround for pages being too long, and it adds 3 controls to every header. It has caused bugs: collapsing the last home section hid the coach FAB in the installed app.
features.dataKeys: localStorage dashboard:sections:v1 {<pageKey>: {order:[slug…], collapsed:{slug:1}}} (device-only)
features.overlapsWith: Page tabs, jump-to-section drawer, home 'More' disclosure, settings.pages
features.automationPotential: Curate short pages so this is not needed; never make the user do layout work.

features.name: Section icons + colours (SECTION_LOOKS)
features.whatItDoes: Prefixes every section title with an emoji chip and a coloured underline, chosen by 24 regex rules on the title text (water 💧 blue, steps 👟 green, sleep 😴 indigo…). Unknown titles get a hashed hue.
features.manualInputs: None
features.valueReturned: Some scannability, but a long page becomes a rainbow of 15+ colours and icons, which adds to the busy feel.
features.dataKeys: None
features.overlapsWith: Skin gradient section titles; home-look section-title overrides
features.automationPotential: Replace with a small fixed category palette (Body / Food / Money / School) defined by the design system.

features.name: Jump-to-section drawer (☰ left-edge tab)
features.whatItDoes: A 22×66px accent tab fixed at the left edge mid-screen on every page with 2 or more sections. It opens a slide-out 'On this page' list that smooth-scrolls to the chosen section.
features.manualInputs: Tap to navigate long pages
features.valueReturned: Helps on 5-screen pages, but it is a third floating element over content and only exists because the pages are too long.
features.dataKeys: None
features.overlapsWith: Section reorder/collapse, page tabs, bottom nav
features.automationPotential: Unneeded once each page fits about 1-1.5 screens

features.name: Page tabs (opt-in, Health only)
features.whatItDoes: With settings.pageTabs=true, Health's sections are grouped into sticky pills (Today / Body / Food / Rest / More) and only one group shows at a time. The last tab is remembered. Nothing is moved in the DOM.
features.manualInputs: Must be discovered and switched on in Settings; then a tap per group
features.valueReturned: The right structural idea (one screen per topic instead of a 5.6-screen scroll), but limited to Health and off by default.
features.dataKeys: settings.pageTabs; localStorage dashboard:ptab:<pageKey>
features.overlapsWith: Section collapse, jump drawer
features.automationPotential: Make segmented 'Today / History' structure the default page pattern in the redesign.

features.name: Eye breaks 20-20-20 (desktop only)
features.whatItDoes: When enabled from a Health card, it runs every N minutes (default 20) within set hours, on desktop only (pointer: fine, width ≥900). It shows a full-screen 'Look away' countdown, a system notification and a loud 3-note chime. The chime repeats while the tab is hidden so it cuts through fullscreen games. Skip and Snooze 5 are offered, and done/skipped counts are logged per day to the cloud.
features.manualInputs: Enable once; then each break is one tap or a 20s wait. It does nothing on the iPhone, where it's configured.
features.valueReturned: A genuine automatic health nudge for long PC sessions. It is irrelevant on the phone, where its card still takes Health page space.
features.dataKeys: localStorage dashboard:eyes:v1 {on, every, rest, from, to, sound}, dashboard:eyes:nextAt; app_state uid:screen.days{YYYY-MM-DD:{done,skipped}}
features.overlapsWith: health.html screen/eyes card; /api/usage writes the same uid:screen row
features.automationPotential: Make it a desktop-only setting and hide it from the phone UI. Its done/skipped stats could feed the weekly recap.

features.name: Cross-device live sync of settings + water
features.whatItDoes: Polls Supabase for water every 4s (home and health) and for settings every 12s on every page, plus on focus, pageshow and visibility change. It applies theme, nav and page-visibility changes live, with a 15s grace window so a fresh local change isn't overwritten.
features.manualInputs: None
features.valueReturned: Phone and PC stay consistent, which the owner explicitly requires (sync must be bidirectional).
features.dataKeys: dashboard:settings:v1 ↔ uid:settings (+_pushAt); po_water_v1 ↔ uid:health; _dashUid
features.overlapsWith: Each page's own sync engine
features.automationPotential: Efficiency fix: pull on focus/visibility only, or use Supabase realtime, instead of a 4s/12s poll. Reuse one Supabase client: xpSupa() calls createClient on every invocation, and the file holds 3+ separate clients.

features.name: Page visibility / Kids-mode guard (settings.pages)
features.whatItDoes: settings.pages {key:false} removes a page's tab and the finance shortcut, and redirects direct URL access back to home. data-mode='kid' enlarges the nav.
features.manualInputs: None after setup
features.valueReturned: The existing switch that lets the redesign retire whole pages without deleting any data.
features.dataKeys: settings.pages {health, fitness, school, habits, food, transport, projects, friends, finance, trends}, settings.mode
features.overlapsWith: onboarding.html page picker; settings.html Pages & Kids mode
features.automationPotential: Use it during the redesign to switch off low-value pages (Projects, Friends, Transport if not automated) as a reversible experiment.

features.name: App-shell plumbing (sw.js cache + auto-update, diag panel, iOS fixes, scroll-fade)
features.whatItDoes: sw.js precaches /, index.html, topbar.js, manifest and icon. It serves network-first and caches every same-origin GET, including /api responses. topbar checks for a new SW on load, focus and resume, then reloads once. Tapping the version 5x (or ?diag=1) opens a green diagnostics panel with FORCE UPDATE. Other pieces: the iOS 16px input anti-zoom rule, pinch and double-tap lock, modal scroll lock, and floating buttons that fade to 18% while scrolling.
features.manualInputs: None
features.valueReturned: Keeps the installed app current. Network-first means every cold open waits on the network, so the app feels slow to open, which hurts a 'glance daily' habit. The scroll-fade exists only because 3 floating widgets cover content.
features.dataKeys: Cache 'dashboard-v2.7.8' (CACHE_VERSION must equal DASHBOARD_VERSION); sessionStorage none
features.overlapsWith: sw.js push handler (see api)
features.automationPotential: Serve the app shell stale-while-revalidate for an instant open with a background refresh. Drop the visible version label. Remove scroll-fade once the buddy and drawer are gone.

pages.purpose: 12 Vercel serverless functions. These are where the app already gets data with no manual input: phone-pushed steps and app usage, live train times, barcode and USDA nutrition lookup, AI food parsing, an AI coach with tools, and the reminder/push backends. They are the raw material for a low-input redesign.
pages.designNotes: The handlers are clean, single-purpose, well commented CommonJS, with friendly plain-text and JSON errors. Problems: 4 of 12 endpoints are dead or broken in production. train-times.js is never called because transport.html uses hand-typed times. subscribe.js, vapid-key.js and send-push.js have no callers. cron-reminders.js returns 500 because NTFY_TOPIC isn't set on Vercel. The Supabase URL, anon key and admin email are hard-coded and duplicated across 4 files. Auth is inconsistent: token in the URL (steps, usage), Supabase JWT plus allowlist (coach, food POST), CRON_SECRET (cron), and none at all (get-reminders and sync-reminders use the service-role key, so anyone with a uid can read or wipe reminders). steps.js and usage.js read and write app_state with the public anon key, which means app_state RLS allows anon access to at least those rows. If anon can SELECT uid:steps, the step token itself is readable; worth checking the RLS policies. The automatic data is also siloed: coach.html's buildContext never loads uid:steps or uid:screen, even though both API files say 'the coach reads this row'.

features.name: /api/steps: automatic step sync (iOS Shortcut bridge)
features.whatItDoes: GET /api/steps?u=<uid>&t=<token>&s=<steps>&tzo=<offset>[&d=YYYY-MM-DD]. It validates a per-account token stored in that account's uid:steps row, works out the local day from the baked-in timezone offset, writes days[date]=steps (latest reading wins, ~400 days kept) and returns a plain-text '✅ 8,421 steps saved for …'.
features.manualInputs: One-time: Health → Steps → Set up, copy the link, then build an iOS Shortcuts personal automation (Get Health Sample: steps → Get Contents of URL), ideally on several time-of-day triggers. After that, zero daily input.
features.valueReturned: Real automatic tracking. health.html shows a ring, weekly bars and average/best with no typing.
features.dataKeys: app_state uid:steps {token, days{YYYY-MM-DD: steps}, goal, updatedAt}
features.overlapsWith: health.html Steps card
features.automationPotential: This is the template for the whole redesign. The same token-plus-GET bridge can ingest anything a Shortcut can read from Apple Health: sleep hours, body weight, active energy, workouts, resting HR, water. Generalise it to /api/ingest?metric=… and retire the manual weight input (health.html #wtInput) and sleep input (#sleepInput). Also add uid:steps to the coach context. Caveat: tzo is fixed at link creation, so Israel's DST switch shifts the day boundary by an hour.

features.name: /api/usage: app open/close screen-time tracking
features.whatItDoes: GET /api/usage?u&t&app=TikTok&e=open|close&tzo. It reuses the steps token. The server pairs open and close events into durations (ignoring sessions under 2s or over 4h), counts opens per app per day and keeps ~120 days.
features.manualInputs: One-time but heavy: 2 Shortcuts automations per tracked app ('App is opened' / 'App is closed', with 'Notify when run' off). Zero daily input afterwards.
features.valueReturned: Real minutes and open counts for the chosen time-sink apps, shown as bars on Health. iOS won't expose total Screen Time, so this is the only automatic signal available. It is not used by the coach or any summary.
features.dataKeys: app_state uid:screen {apps{YYYY-MM-DD:{<App>:{ms, opens}}}, open{<App>: ts}, days{date:{done,skipped}} (eye-break stats share the row), updatedAt}
features.overlapsWith: Eye-break stats (same row); health.html usage card
features.automationPotential: Surface it as one line in a daily or weekly brief ('TikTok 1h12m yesterday, +20% vs avg') and add it to coach context, instead of a dedicated card the owner has to scroll to.

features.name: /api/train-times: live Israel Railways routes (currently UNUSED)
features.whatItDoes: Proxies rail.co.il GetRoutes and returns the next 6 trains (depart, arrive, platform, delay, transfers) with a 90s CDN cache. ?stations=1 lists station IDs and ?debug=1 dumps the raw response. Default stations from=2300 to=8600 are hard-coded.
features.manualInputs: None if wired. Today transport.html ignores it: the owner types departure times comma-separated ('Check rail.co.il… when the schedule changes seasonally') and arrival is assumed to be +22 min.
features.valueReturned: Nothing right now, because no page calls it. Wired up, it would give live departures and delays for the Rosh HaAyin North → Herzliya commute with zero input.
features.dataKeys: None server-side (transport.html stores its manual schedule locally)
features.overlapsWith: transport.html manual train schedule plus its own ntfy reminders
features.automationPotential: Wire transport (or a home 'next train' line) to this endpoint and delete the manual schedule editor. Before relying on it: (1) it builds Date/Hour/Minute from the server clock, which on Vercel is UTC, so it likely queries 2-3h in the past and the wrong date late in the evening; compute Asia/Jerusalem time instead. (2) Look up the real station IDs via ?stations=1. (3) Verify the unofficial rail.co.il API still responds.

features.name: /api/barcode: Open Food Facts lookup
features.whatItDoes: GET ?code=<digits>. Returns product name, brand and per-100g nutrients, converting OFF's grams to the app's mg/µg units (sodium, vitamins…) and keeping unknown fields as off_<name>_g. It gives clear messages for not-found and no-nutrition cases.
features.manualInputs: Per packaged food: scan the barcode, then choose the portion in grams
features.valueReturned: No hand-typing of macros for packaged foods. A portion is still required.

features.name: /api/food GET: USDA FoodData Central search
features.whatItDoes: GET ?q=…. Needs USDA_API_KEY. Returns up to 20 foods with every USDA nutrient per 100g, lab-analysed generic entries first and branded last.
features.manualInputs: Per food item: type a search, pick a result, enter grams
features.valueReturned: Precise micronutrients (iron, vitamin D, B12…). That's thorough, but probably more detail than the owner acts on.
features.dataKeys: None server-side; env USDA_API_KEY
features.overlapsWith: Barcode, AI estimate
features.automationPotential: Keep it as a precision fallback; don't make it the default entry path.

features.name: /api/food POST: AI text-to-macros
features.whatItDoes: POST {text, token}. Checks the Supabase session plus admin or ai:allowlist, then sends the sentence to Claude Haiku 4.5 (or Gemini 2.5 Flash via OpenRouter). Returns up to 12 items [{name, qty_desc, kcal, protein_g, carbs_g, fat_g}].

features.name: /api/coach: AI coach with dashboard-editing tools
features.whatItDoes: POST messages plus a client-built context JSON. Uses a persona prompt ('direct, practical, under ~180 words, use their real numbers'). Tools: set_nutrition_targets, replace_meal_plan, add_meal, set_gym_exercise, add_gym_exercise, set_water_setup, each confirmed with Apply/Skip in the browser. On Anthropic it uses prompt-cached context (default claude-haiku-4-5-20251001); on OpenRouter it falls back to free models. Gated to admin plus allowlist.

This turns the app from input collector into info giver. (2) Add logging tools (log_meal, log_water, log_weight, log_sleep, add_goal, complete_habit) so natural language replaces forms. (3) Add the missing context: uid:steps, uid:screen, finance, school/exams, transport. (4) One chat surface instead of three.

features.name: Reminders backend (cron-reminders, get-reminders, sync-reminders)
features.whatItDoes: index.html sends the reminder list to sync-reminders, which deletes all of the user's rows and re-inserts them into the 'reminders' table. cron-job.org calls cron-reminders every minute. Reminders whose time_local matches the current time in their timezone are POSTed to ntfy.sh/<NTFY_TOPIC>. get-reminders loads the list on page load.
features.manualInputs: Once: create reminders (title, time) on home, install the ntfy app and subscribe to the topic
features.valueReturned: Push is how an app 'comes to you' instead of being a duty to open. Currently zero: NTFY_TOPIC isn't set on Vercel, so the cron returns 500. Other problems: index.html runs a second, client-side ntfy scheduler with a user-typed topic (two reminder systems); the cron ignores repeat_daily=false; every user's reminders go to one topic; get and sync have no auth.

There is no web-push sender anywhere.
features.manualInputs: None. No page calls /api/subscribe, /api/vapid-key or /api/send-push.

features.overlapsWith: ntfy reminder system
features.automationPotential: Either finish it (a web-push sender in the cron) and retire ntfy, or delete it. One notification channel, not two half-built ones.

crossCuttingObservations:
1. topbar.js is where the 'more and more' piled up. It is 220KB, injected into every page, and about half of it is decoration or gamification rather than function: the buddy is ~38KB, XP ~31KB, skins, surface styles and home looks are 50KB+. Git history agrees: 165 of the 246 commits touch topbar.js, almost all in June-July 2026. The old screenshots (ss_home.png, ss_health.png) show a calm 3-tab app; today every page carries a sticky top bar, a 10-tab nav, a skin banner, a pulsing coach FAB, a floating buddy and a left-edge drawer tab.

2. The duty loop lives in the shared chrome. Every page reinforces logging for its own sake:
- '+20 XP Daily check-in' just for opening the app.
- XP per tap, with a toast on every log.
- A streak-freeze shop and 15 achievement badges.
- Skins locked behind XP levels (settings.html SKIN_LOCK).
- Level, weekly XP and streak broadcast to friends every 2 minutes.

All of it rewards how many things the owner enters; none of it rewards what they learn. That is the mechanism behind 'felt like a duty'. Cutting XP, badges, freezes, the buddy and the friends broadcast removes the pressure without losing any real data (uid:xp can stay in the DB).

3. Five features exist only because pages are too long: section collapse/reorder, the jump-to-section drawer, opt-in page tabs, the scroll-fade for floating buttons, and the home 'More' disclosure from v2.7.7. They treat the symptom. The redesign should shorten pages (about 1 screen each, Today/History segments) and then delete these.

4. Design never converged because there is a theme engine instead of a design. The appearance axes multiply out to ~57k combinations: light/dark × 8 accents × 6 skins × 11 surface styles × 6 home looks × 4 structures × 3 radii × 3 font sizes. They are implemented as !important overrides on legacy class names, with up to 6 infinite animations running and a rainbow of auto-coloured section headers. Recommendation: one finished visual system, dark and cinematic-like (serif greeting plus date, hairline glass cards, one accent, tabular numerals). Keep at most light/dark and an accent. The old settings fields can simply be ignored, so no migration is needed.

5. The low-input raw material already exists but is unused or siloed:
- **Steps** (/api/steps) and **app usage** (/api/usage) arrive automatically from iOS Shortcuts.
- **Live trains** (/api/train-times) exist, yet transport.html makes the owner type departure times by hand.
- **Food:** barcode lookup, USDA search, and the one-sentence AI estimator (food POST) all exist.
- **The coach** has tools that edit plans.

Concrete moves:
- Generalise the steps.js token+GET bridge into /api/ingest for Apple Health sleep, weight, active energy, workouts and water. That kills the biggest manual inputs (health.html #wtInput, #sleepInput).
- Add uid:steps and uid:screen (plus finance and school) to the coach context. coach.html's buildContext omits them today, despite comments saying otherwise.
- Give the coach logging tools (log_meal, log_water, log_weight, log_sleep, add_goal) so a single home 'quick log' sentence replaces forms.
- Have the coach write a proactive 3-line daily brief and a Sunday recap. The buddy's recap logic is a ready starting point.

6. Notifications are what would make the app come to the owner, but they are split and broken:
- Server cron via NTFY_TOPIC is currently 500ing because the env var isn't set.
- A second client-side ntfy scheduler runs in index.html with a user-typed topic.
- Web push (VAPID keys set, SW handler present) has no subscribe caller and no sender.

Pick one channel and finish it. Native web push works for installed iPhone PWAs and needs no ntfy app. Use it for data-driven nudges and briefs, not just static reminders.

7. Things to keep: the one-tap water pill (best input-to-value ratio), cross-device sync (the owner's hard requirement, but switch the 4s/12s polling to focus-based pulls or realtime, and reuse one Supabase client instead of xpSupa creating a new one per call), settings.pages (lets the redesign retire pages reversibly without deleting data), the greeting hero, and the SW auto-update. Make the shell stale-while-revalidate: network-first makes every cold open wait on the network, which works against a quick daily glance.

8. Bugs and risks to verify live, per the owner's 'verify in the real app' rule:
- train-times.js builds its query time from the server clock (UTC on Vercel), so it probably asks for trains 2-3h in the past.
- Its default station IDs (2300→8600) may not be the owner's route.
- cron-reminders ignores repeat_daily=false.
- get-reminders and sync-reminders are unauthenticated and use the service-role key.
- steps.js and usage.js use the anon key for server reads and writes. That implies anon RLS access to app_state; check whether other users' rows or step tokens are anon-readable.
- CLAUDE.md's env-var list omits VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY and VAPID_SUBJECT.

Data keys to preserve in any redesign:
- dashboard:settings:v1 ↔ uid:settings
- po_water_v1 ↔ uid:health.po_water_v1
- dashboard:xp:v1 ↔ uid:xp
- uid:steps, uid:screen
- the reminders and push_subscriptions tables
- ai:allowlist
- the profiles and activity tables
- device-only: dashboard:nav:v1, dashboard:sections:v1, dashboard:eyes:v1, dashboard:ptab:*, buddy_chat, buddy_affinity, buddy_pos, buddy_recap_week, friend_profile, _dashUid
